newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures firm on technicals, APIs.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures firm on technicals, APIs.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were firmer on Monday in what traders said was a technical move backed up by mildly supportive weekly inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute.
May Brent was 20 cents a barrel firmer at 0934 GMT and stood at $18.13, after appearing to have broken through the first level of resistance at $18.10.
April gas oil, which expires on Thursday, was $1.25 a tonne firmer at $164 while May gas oil was $1 up at $165.00.
News that an Iraqi plane with pilgrims flew to Mecca in defiance of U.N. sanctions also exerted a positive, if minimal influence.
"Support has come from technicals and the API data and maybe a teeny bit from the Iraq news," one broker said.
Gasoline stocks in the U.S. fell by 1.22 million barrels in the week to April 4, while production climbed 632,000 barrels per day to 7.67 million, the API weekly report said.
Technical analysts had earlier expected the market to range higher on Wednesday.

The market is well supported at $17.65, the lowest point of the recent trading range, and traders said that beyond the $18.10 level lies resistance starting at around $18.36 and ending with the top of a chart gap at $18.50.
Gas oil faces chart gap resistance at $166.75, according to Nicholas Wilson at MeesPierson Derivatives in the Isle of Man.

Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives in London, using their Market Profile technical chart technique, said of the April gas oil contract: "We look to buy again on dips to $162 and/or join breaks higher, $164 being the first level, waiting for $167 for profit taking or $165.50 for the conservative day trade.
